title: Billy Hicks and the Sizzling Six
summary: Billy Hicks's band was the first local Black band at the St. Regis; earlier, around 1931-32, he took a band to Haiti.

bands.name: Billy Hicks and the Sizzling Six

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: One thing I just remembered that you forgot was your experience with Billy Hicks.
Oh, Billy Hicks and the Sizzling Six. He was known as the Sizzling Six. He was the first local Colored
band to play St. Regis. I was in Europe when that happened. But prior to that, it was back in the Thirties, the early Thirties, about '31 or '32, Billy Hicks, Joe Vidas(?), Quinton Harrington and...

By the way, he's supposed to write me a letter and tell me the exact year, exactly... He took a band to Haiti. And in Haiti there was a gentleman by the name of Eydan(?), who came from Amsterdam Avenue and 106th Street, somewhere around that way, who put up the first electric sign in Haiti. It was a little small theatre right in the park, in the little rotunda, a little round place where the band used to play. It was at a little bungalow which they called the first theatre in Port Au Prince, the first motion picture theatre in Port Au Prince. And he put up an electric sign. Prior to that, they didn't have anything like that.
